final_lessons: Under tight step budgets, faster-converging optimizers with adequate learning rates tend to win.
Higher effective learning rates (via lr and momentum) help under tight step budgets.
Adaptive optimizers with higher learning rates converge fastest under tight budgets.
Momentum-boosted SGD with moderate lr tends to outperform tiny-lr baselines.
The highest-learning-rate adaptive optimizer generally converges best under tight budgets.
Model capacity (wide + residual) appears to matter more than learning rate for this task.
When capacity is comparable, a substantially higher learning rate is decisive.
Large width dominates outcomes for this univariate task.
Among equal-capacity models, adaptive AdamW edges out SGD under tight budgets.
Large width remains the decisive factor even against higher-lr narrow models.
